change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: canManage() is granted by the VIEW scope, so a view-only all-groups permission lets the admin create groups
findings.body: `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so any `view` permission on the Groups resource type makes it true. `GroupsResource` guards creating a top-level group with `auth.groups().requireManage()` (GroupsResource.java:181). The result: an admin who was only given `view` on all groups can create top-level groups (and anything else gated on `canManage()`). Every other manage check in this class asks only for MANAGE (`canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79), and so does V1 `canManage()` (GroupPermissions.java:275). Change it to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, and fix the interface Javadoc (GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:75-76), which describes the same wrong rule. `testManageAllGroups` only grants MANAGE, so this case is never tested.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the resource's id where the group id (the resource name) is needed
findings.body: V2 group resources are named after the group id, and their own id is generated: `getOrCreateResource` calls `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)` with `name = group.getId()` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121, 185). This loop passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which calls `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (line 141). That lookup never matches, so evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource. The loop then also adds resource ids to `granted`. That set is used as group ids for `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` (UsersResource.java:448-450, BruteForceUsersResource.java:147-149) and for `getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)` (UsersResource.java:398/425/430). An admin with per-group VIEW_MEMBERS then gets the wrong user count, and the search is filtered by group ids that do not exist, with no error. The sibling `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` uses `resource.getName()` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:138-140). Use `groupResource.getName()` in both places.

findings.title: VIEW_MEMBERS tests never check users/count or the group-id filter
findings.body: `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` only checks the user search. That search still passes when `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` returns wrong ids, because `toRepresentation` filters each user with `canView` again (UsersResource.java:460). Asserting `users().count()` for myadmin after granting VIEW_MEMBERS would catch the id/name mismatch at GroupPermissionsV2.java:122. A test that grants only `view` on all groups and then expects group creation to be FORBIDDEN would catch the `canManage()` scope bug.

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc points to the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but the implementations check `canManageMembers` (GroupPermissions.java:376-379). Also, the `@return` at line 145 says "Stream of IDs", but the method returns a `Set`.

contracts.action: V2 group-scoped user search: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission feeds UserModel.GROUPS session attribute
contracts.before_after: Sibling adds resource.getName() (the object id); new code adds groupResource.getId() (generated resource id) and evaluates by findByName(resourceId)
contracts.visible_effect: Wrong user counts and a wrongly filtered user search for admins with group VIEW_MEMBERS

contracts.before_after: Before, the filter ran twice; now it runs once, in toRepresentation

contracts.action: V2 canManage() gate for top-level group creation
contracts.equivalent_path: V1 GroupPermissions.canManage() and V2 canManage(GroupModel), both MANAGE only
contracts.before_after: New V2 canManage() also accepts the VIEW scope
contracts.visible_effect: An admin with view-only all-groups permission can create groups

summary: This PR adds V2 fine-grained admin permissions for the Groups resource type. I found two defects in GroupPermissionsV2. (1) `canManage()` is granted by the VIEW scope, so a view-only all-groups permission lets an admin create top-level groups. That is a blocker. (2) `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` uses `groupResource.getId()` where it needs `getName()`, the group id. As a result, the group-id filter for user search and the users count are computed from ids that don't exist. Neither case is tested. Two Javadoc slips are minor. The other refactors (inlining canManageDefault/canViewDefault, removing the duplicate canView filter, renaming getGroupsWithViewPermission) behave the same as before.
